newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Access sees Australian unemployment falling.
newsitem.headline: Access sees Australian unemployment falling.

text.p: Economics consultancy Access Economics said on Monday that it expected Australia's unemployment rate to fall to about 7.4 percent in mid-1998 from its current, stagnant level at 8.7 percent.
Access said in its latest quarterly report that a large proportion of the expected fall in unemployment would arise from strong growth in part-time jobs.
"Unemployment is expected to begin to improve from now on -- the next clear move will be down," Access said in its March quarter Five Year Business Outlook.
"Much of the coming fall in unemployment will be attributable to a lift in part-time jobs," it said.
But Access warned that the labour market would not improve significantly until a forecast housing sector pick-up in the second half of calendar 1997.
"1997 will be a year of good news on the labour market, but not quite as good as some analysts expect," it said.
"The pick-up evident in the second half of 1996 has not yet translated into increased hours worked," Access said.
"It will not do so in a convincing fashion until the housing sector reaches lift-off in the second half of 1997, taking a chunk of manufacturing with it," it said.
The participation rate was also forecast to rise, in line with the expected labour force growth, after largely remaining flat in calendar 1996.
In March, Australian unemployment was at 8.7 percent down from 8.8 percent in the previous month.
The participation rate fell to 63.3 percent from 63.7 percent in the previous two months.
"For the first time since the late 1980s, wages may well move sufficiently ahead of productivity to be another factor in the expected CPI (consumer price index) rebound in 1998."

The Reserve Bank of Australia has set an underlying inflation rate target of between two and three percent throughout 1998. March quarter inflation data is due out on Wednesday. In the year to December 1996, underlying inflation rose 2.1 percent, while the CPI lifted 1.5 percent.
Access said increasing wage pressure were likely to push inflation higher with both headline and underlying rates of inflation forecast to move over three percent by the end of calendar 1998.
"We remain of the view that end-1997 will see inflation begin to rise as the bulk of the (currency) appreciation has run its course, demand is picking up and wage pressures loom," Access said.
It said the outcome of the Australian Council of Trade Unions "living wage" case, to be announced on Tuesday, was likely to contribute to an acceleration in wages.
